item.title: Post-contest reflections
item.content:encoded:
My prediction with this contest is that we'll only get a small number gems from this. Someone will pull a very successful gimmick, possibly making up for being lower than 173's word count if they aimed for it, and will win with that. That one will stay and possibly rack up a lot of upvotes after the contest because of its fame. The vast majority of skips who aimed for below 173's word count, excluding ones that pulled a successful gimmick, will fail. Those closer to the 500 word limit will probably have a better chance of lasting after the contest, but that depends on the author's talent with short short fiction.

That seems a pretty good summary, Fantem.

item.content:encoded:
HERE ARE THE WINNERS OF THE 2015 SHORT CONTEST!

1st Place: ●●|●●●●●|●●|● by LurkD, with a landslide victory at +202 votes.
2nd Place: SCP-2915 by Djoric at +89 votes
3rd Place: SCP-2771 by Petrograd at +78 votes

Wordcounts were tallied independently by Cimmerian and me. They ended up being either the same, or near enough as not to make a difference for bonus, winner ranking, or qualification purposes. Kaktus made a code to pull the page votes at midnight at the ending period. Any questions?

(Special shout-outs to Dmatix for writing the shortest entry in the contest, to MrWrong, Zolgamax, and Davsto for coming in at 500 words exactly, and DolphinSlugchugger for writing an entry in the waning hours of the opening period and submitting it at exactly one minute until closing.)

Also, a big shout out to everyone else who entered. Y'all made some really cool pieces happen, and put an enormous amount of quality material onto the site. I'm thrilled with the reception and entries this contest got.

This page will be converted into a hub for the contest entries, and the front page feature will happen in the future.
